experiments.title: Production fusion with two ASR systems and no LLM
experiments.question: Can the per-column composition win be delivered in production with TWO ASR systems instead of three, given that whole-window selection with two was measured at 0.1349 and lost, and that with N=2 no 2-of-3 majority exists to break identity disagreements?
experiments.next_action: Stage 0 of the spec, which costs nothing: score 3 pairs x 2 bases x 3 arms (P0/P1/P2) on the already-cached 247-window substrate, leave-one-city-out with every threshold fitted out-of-fold, plus the per-pair diagnostics (correct-token union coverage, both-wrong rate, exclusive-correct by producer, pairwise alignment-conditional oracle, KEEP-minus-DROP edit cost per singleton direction, conditional accuracy on identity disagreements, stability by city and meeting). Before any of that, one cheap probe: call Soniox stt-async-v5 on a single window and record which per-word fields it actually returns, since every timestamp and confidence figure this project holds for Soniox is stt-rt-v4 and the two must not be mixed.
caveats: NOTHING HERE IS MEASURED FOR N=2. Two-system per-column composition has never been run in this project or quoted from outside it. The design extrapolates from the three-system result of exp-2026-08-16-composition-over-selection (0.1201 -> 0.1005). The only measured two-system number is whole-window SELECTION at 0.1349, which lost to the best single system.

The chosen pair (artifact-ct2-fixed + Soniox stt-async-v5) is the COST-CONSTRAINED pair, not the accuracy-optimal pair. Scribe v2 dominates our adapter on WER, deletions and substitutions and loses only on insertions; it is excluded because no ElevenLabs credential exists in this environment (established by exp-2026-08-16-gold-set) and because confidence must come from the same decode pass as the text (exp-2026-08-18-conf-substrate, 0 of 133 windows text-joinable). Marginal error rates do not demonstrate complementary errors; only the Stage 0 pairwise diagnostics can.

Every Soniox timestamp and confidence figure the project holds is stt-rt-v4 (artifact-soniox-rt-tokens-2026-08-16): 96.8% column coverage, 0.058 s median turn-edge distance, AUROC 0.8167. Production runs stt-async-v5 and the caveat on that artifact forbids mixing them. None of those numbers may be assumed for the production input.

The occupancy default is DROP with a restore gate, which optimises agreement-with-OpenCouncil. It is probably the WRONG default for fidelity-to-audio: 40.8% of Soniox insertions and 23.7% of ours are real speech the published reference omits (exp-2026-08-17-insertion-fidelity). The spec keeps the two metrics separate and keeps every dropped span in the output rather than resolving the disagreement.

A calibrated-confidence identity tie-break is an arm, not an assumption. The nearest measurement is arm A of exp-2026-08-16-w-rt-confidence: 750 firings, dWER -0.00035, CI [-0.00105,+0.00027] includes zero, both rate gates fail narrowly; two sibling arms never fired in any of ten folds. Raw cross-vendor confidence comparison is forbidden.

Stage 0 is the seventh pass over the same 247 windows. Cross-fitting does not undo repeated analyst exposure, so it selects a configuration and can never supply the shipping claim. Stage 1 requires audio this project has never scored; the 16 locked evaluation windows stay sealed and the gold set has spent its one confirmatory pass.

The structural ceiling of exp-2026-08-17-majority-error-taxonomy applies at least as hard here: 27.7% of wrong majorities are definitely not a selection problem and 39.6% are not cleanly attributable to selection.
Speaker-attribution accuracy of the emitted schema is UNMEASURED. There is no ground truth outside the gold set, where the number that means something is 0.714 recall inside overlap.

Section 6 (confusion network for an LLM, extra-speaker detection) is explicitly future work and nothing in it is implemented or measured. Shaped by codex job e2771f4c; the merge rule was rewritten from per-column tiers to base-plus-disagreement-islands by codex job 8dbcf232.

experiments.title: Training-set WER for the corrected adapter
experiments.question: What WER does artifact-ct2-fixed achieve on the labels it trained on, and does the correction/no_edit split distinguish failure to fit from validation generalization?
experiments.conclusion: On an outcome-blind frozen simple-random sample of 300 rows from the exact 28,967-row control training parquet (136 meetings, 9 cities, 861 s audio, 2,368 normalized reference tokens), artifact-ct2-fixed scores training WER 0.1313 [0.1056,0.1619 meeting-clustered 95%], versus 0.2728 for artifact-ct2-base-large-v3 on the exact same sample and stack. The paired base-minus-fixed delta is +0.1415 [0.1138,0.1725]: adaptation cuts substitutions, deletions and insertions, with no leave-one-row sign reversal and the largest row carrying 3.0% of net gain. It learns corrections strongly: correction WER falls 0.4471 -> 0.2261 (-0.2210 point estimate); no_edit falls 0.1020 -> 0.0385 (-0.0635). Therefore failure to learn corrections is ruled out on this sample, although residual correction WER remains high. Against the matched fixed validation decode at 0.1548, train-minus-validation is -0.0235 descriptively; short training clips versus long validation windows confound that gap.
experiments.decision: Every future training run reports this frozen 300-row training sample and the 39-window validation set at comparable checkpoints, including S/D/I and correction/no_edit slices. Training WER is diagnostic and never selects an arm. The next CPU audit targets residual correction errors by boundary status, duration, overlap and category, with blind listening in high-loss strata. Since the paired base contrast shows strong learning on both slices, the first new training mechanism remains dense-30s packing; the audit decides whether it also needs a protected label/boundary lane. The optional July-broken decode remains skipped.
caveats: Agreement with training labels, not fidelity to audio. A low number can mean memorisation of flawed labels; the 22.6% correction-row result does not prove those labels are wrong.
The paired base contrast proves the adapter learned its training labels, not that the learning generalises. The validation set remains the arm-selection endpoint.
The frozen sample is 300 of 28,967 rows. Its interval covers sampling and between-meeting variation, not training-run or decoder nondeterminism.

The direct validation reference is the exact representation-matched served-config arm R at 0.1548. The old 0.1589 raw segment-string join and the 0.1556-0.1584 A_s13/A_s29/A_s47 artifact range are deliberately not used for the gap.
Training rows are short isolated clips while validation rows are long windows, so the -0.0235 gap does not isolate in-sample generalization.
Transcript, audio and hypotheses remain under ~/.cache/oc-public/training-wer-2026-08-n300/. Aggregates only entered git; zero GPU, zero paid API and zero sealed holdout access.

experiments.title: Clean-data filter ladder CPU census
experiments.question: Can the current external-pack supply be filtered into a demonstrably cleaner equal-hours training arm without removing the names, fast speech and hard examples the model needs to learn?
experiments.conclusion: CAPACITY PASSES; WHOLESALE STRICT FILTERING FAILS THE REPRESENTATION PREFLIGHT. Across the current hparl2-v2, stoma-v2, cv-v2 and eurospeech-v2 packs, L0/L1 contain 50,848 rows / 111.027 h and are identical because every packed row already has a Soniox witness. Frozen L2 (alignment >=0.95, 1.5-30 s, >=3 normalized tokens, no clipped edge) retains 30,044 rows / 60.069 h: 59.1% of rows and 54.1% of hours. It retains only 51.5% of the known-roster-name proxy rows, 48.9% of the broader capitalization proxy, 43.8% of fast-speech rows and zero hard examples by construction. L3 is measurable only for EuroSpeech through its existing Whisper-Turbo ds_wer and retains 1,063 rows / 4.146 h; it is an easy-for-Whisper proxy, not guaranteed-clean data.
experiments.decision: SCREEN - STOP for the raw L0-versus-L2-wholesale arm: do not spend GPU on it. The next defensible variant is a new treatment, not a threshold tweak: blind retained/rejected audio audit by source and frozen name/fast/hard strata, followed by an L2 clean core plus a protected audited hard/name lane. Any later training comparison must be equal-hours within source, with identical optimizer updates, recipe, decode and paired seeds 13/29/47. The in-domain OpenCouncil backbone remains outside this witness ladder because independent-witness coverage is selective and would confound label quality with selection.
caveats: This is a CPU census and representation preflight, not a model result. It can veto the measured arm but cannot establish that any retained row is audio-faithful or that filtering improves validation WER.

Name, fast-speech and hard-example labels are frozen metadata proxies, not ground truth. The roster proxy misses external and inflected names; capitalization is noisy and may reflect generated casing.
HParl and EuroSpeech overlap in source domain and must not be silently combined without deduplication. All retention and equal-hours targets remain source-specific.
L3 has a second witness only for EuroSpeech, and that witness is Whisper-Turbo. Its 4.146 h preferentially select examples already easy for the model family being adapted.
No validation, test or sealed holdout data were read. Aggregates only entered git; zero GPU and zero paid API.

experiments.title: Training versus inference 30-second occupancy audit
experiments.question: Are the single-utterance clips used by the control training recipe distributionally mismatched to the nearly full 30-second windows seen at inference, and can the same rows be repacked densely without loss?
experiments.conclusion: YES: THE AUDIO-SUPPORT MISMATCH IS LARGE AND A DENSE ARM IS CONSTRUCTION-FEASIBLE. The exact control-A training parquet has 28,967 rows / 22.4725 raw annotation-span hours. Its intended clips average 3.553 s, or 11.84% encoder occupancy, with 88.16% mean digital padding and 90.40% median padding; 87.6% of raw-span time lies in the first five seconds and no clip reaches 25-30 s. Replaying the existing 247-window inference cache yields 1,148 encoder windows at 91.19% mean source-audio occupancy, 100% median, with 82.6% full 30-second windows. The mean inference-minus-training occupancy gap is 79.34 percentage points. The existing greedy packer forms 3,877 packs with 26.15/27.54 s mean/median duration, 93.27% in 20-30 s, 87.16% mean occupancy and zero dropped utterances or accounting failures.
experiments.decision: SCREEN - ADVANCE at the CPU feasibility stage only. If the user separately authorizes GPU, compare A (current single-utterance clips) against B (the same rows in dense packs, without timestamp tokens), holding base checkpoint, optimizer budget, sampler exposure and paired seeds fixed under docs/decisions/training-evidence.md. Do not retest inference segmentation unless B passes the training screen. No WER or deletion improvement is claimed from construction feasibility.
caveats: The 2.793-second inherited value is an annotation-span proxy, not frame-level VAD speech. The intended 3.553-second clip estimate follows the trainer boundaries and padding but precedes the final clamp to source-recording end because the pod-built WAV cache is unavailable locally.
Inference audio occupancy measures available source audio. Its emitted-word positions are model outputs and are descriptive only; they are not ground-truth speech occupancy.

The inference side reuses an already-read 247-window benchmark cache, not the frozen 39-window validation set and not either sealed holdout. It establishes a deployment-shape mismatch, not transport to a new population.

The dense simulation proves construction and accounting only. It does not isolate whether dense audio, silence layout or timestamp supervision changes model quality until a controlled training arm runs.
Aggregates only entered git; zero training, zero GPU, zero paid API and zero sealed holdout access.

experiments.title: How a training arm earns more budget or a claim of improvement
experiments.question: How should training arms be screened, promoted and confirmed when the inherited 2.1-WER-point number was never a variance estimate for the current evaluation harness?
experiments.conclusion: THE 2.1-POINT NUMBER WAS MISNAMED: it is the range of three old paired treatment effects, not a seed variance or standard deviation. Re-scoring the three existing full-recipe controls A_s13/A_s29/A_s47 on the current 39-window frozen validation set gives WER 0.15557/0.15582/0.15842, a range of 0.285 points and sample SD 0.158 points. A second seed-13 run differs from artifact-adapter-fixed by -0.336 points, descriptively. One window supplies 23 of the 34 net errors between the best and worst seed, 67.6% of the range. Control-only SD cannot size a paired treatment confirmation: the paired-effect SD must come from the 300-step matched pilot.
experiments.decision: Adopt the successive-halving evidence ladder in docs/decisions/training-evidence.md. Three paired seeds are mandatory for a 300-step large-v3 SCREEN; use their paired deltas to calculate the seed count for 80% power and a two-sided 95% interval. Underpowered arms are labelled SCREEN - ADVANCE or SCREEN - STOP, never wins or negative findings. Primary endpoint is frozen-validation WER; any higher mean deletion rate fails; insertion delta must stay below +0.0005; leave-one-window-out may not reverse the sign and no window may carry over 25% of net gain. Every new GPU stage requires explicit user approval. Fresh external research, when needed, runs through ssh laptop and the Grok Research skill on the MacBook.
caveats: Only three seed outcomes. The 0.158-point SD is imprecise and is raw-control variation, not paired treatment-effect variation.
The same-seed comparison has matching run_meta fields and different weight hashes but no batch-order or hardware attestation, so it is descriptive total run nondeterminism only.
A single window carries 67.6% of the net best-to-worst seed range. No general seed-effect magnitude is claimed without the dominance caveat.
Agreement-with-OpenCouncil on 39 validation windows / 31 meetings / 11,911 tokens, common local CPU int8 stack and common per-window decoder seeds. The seven temporal holdouts remained sealed.
Hypothesis text and CT2 calibration builds stay under ~/.cache/oc-public/seed-calibration-2026-08/. Aggregates only entered git. Zero GPU and zero paid API.

experiments.title: How much of a scored insertion is speech our own published reference omits
experiments.question: Of the words a system emits that the published OpenCouncil transcript does not have - the words agreement-WER charges as insertions - how many are supported by the human who listened, and how many of those sit on gold occurrences the published text cannot be reading?
experiments.conclusion: A MEANINGFUL SHARE OF SCORED INSERTIONS IS NOT SYSTEM ERROR, AND THE SHARE IS LARGER FOR THE SYSTEM WITH THE HIGHEST INSERTION RATE. On the frozen gold set (26 scored cells in the primary core-envelope region, 6 meetings / 6 cities, 999 certain gold tokens, 905 published tokens), 18 of 76 (23.7% [0.0417,0.5714]) of artifact-adapter-fixed's insertions and 53 of 130 (40.8% [0.2895,0.5424]) of Soniox stt-rt-v4's are matched to a certain gold occurrence that the published text fails to match under EVERY minimum-cost alignment. A further 36.8% and 12.3% are UNDECIDABLE - the token's plausible window is not wholly inside annotated, text-certain coverage - and only 31.6% and 28.5% are unsupported. The four classes are mutually exclusive and exhaust the population: the residual 7.9% (6 of 76) and 14.6% (19 of 130) are gold-supported but sit on occurrences the published text DOES match in every optimal alignment, i.e. duplications and alignment artefacts, not reference omission. Full ADP census 76 = 18 forced-unmatched + 0 possible-but-not-forced + 6 PUB-matched + 28 undecidable + 24 unsupported; SNX 130 = 53 + 5 + 19 + 16 + 37, i.e. the forced/possible band is 58 vs 53 for SNX and empty for ADP. As rates: of ADP's 0.0840 measured insertion rate, 0.0199 [0.0009,0.0491] is reference-omission-consistent, at most 0.0508 counting every undecidable; of SNX's 0.1436, it is 0.0586 [0.0181,0.1247], at most 0.0818. | THE CLASS THE CUT F3 FAMILY WOULD HAVE DELETED IS THE WORST CASE FOR DELETING: insertions ECHOED by the other system within 1.5 s are 0.720 (ADP, n=25) and 0.796 (SNX, n=54) gold-supported and 0.480 / 0.407 PUB-unmatched-forced, at every tau_w in {0.75,1.5,3.0}. Dropping words two systems both heard would have improved WER by reproducing editorial omission. The llm-composer draft's argument for cutting F3 now has a number. | THE DIRECT OVERLAP TEST, on a GOLD-occurrence denominator rather than an insertion-conditioned one: gold occurrences whose block touches simultaneous speech go unmatched by the published text at 25/74 = 0.338 [0.189,0.486] against 140/925 = 0.151 [0.089,0.243] outside - the parent study's pipeline-loss finding recapitulated. The insertion-conditioned overlap split CANNOT answer this (0 ADP and 7 SNX insertions in strict overlap) and the adjacency variant runs the other way and is exploratory only. | SEPARATE ESTIMAND, never merged: the published text's own gold-unsupported tokens are 27/999 = 0.0270 [0.0041,0.0519] - fidelity-to-audio, not agreement.
experiments.decision: Quote this as DESCRIPTION of this frozen set only. Two statements about the 247-window benchmark are permitted and no more: (a) Soniox's PUB-relative insertion rate is descriptively higher than the adapter's in both datasets, ratio 1.71 here against 3.3 there, datasets not exchangeable; (b) benchmark insertion headroom must NOT be equated with hallucination headroom, so the 2.43-point gap between W's 0.03743 and the column oracle's 0.01312 is not wholly a catalogue of invented words. FORBIDDEN: applying 23.7% or 40.8% to the benchmark, producing corrected benchmark rates, revising 2.43 numerically, or inferring anything about W or Scribe. The primary is conditional on the shipped midpoint PUB-boundary rule and is NOT invariant to it (wholly_contained triples the insertion count). Regions are separate estimands and are never summed. Any future insertion-gated arm should be read knowing the gate is partly punishing recovery of real speech; that is a reason to report the gate's composition, not a reason to loosen it. The open work item is unchanged from the parent study: a Scribe v2 credential and a run of W on this audio.
caveats: W WAS NOT RUN and cannot be: no ElevenLabs credential in this environment, same wall as exp-2026-08-16-gold-set. Covered systems are artifact-adapter-fixed on the local CPU endpoint and Soniox stt-rt-v4, the FREE realtime path - not the paid stt-async-v5. The published text is the REFERENCE and therefore has no insertions against itself.

27 cells, 6 meetings, ONE MEETING PER CITY, so meeting and city are fully confounded. Meeting-clustered intervals over 6 clusters are descriptive; one that excludes zero is NOT statistical significance and no p-value is quoted.

ONE ANNOTATOR, one pass, no second annotator. The intervals cover sampling and between-meeting variation only - the annotator's own error is in none of them. The reference is prefilled from a Whisper-family system and corrected, and ADP is Whisper-family.

The 17 spans the annotator judged as lost speech in the parent study were never written into the frozen reference, so the gold knowingly under-covers and every not_supported count is an over-count by an unmeasured amount.

SAMOTHRAKI DOMINATES THE INSERTION SUPPLY: 54 of ADP's 76 insertions and 74 of SNX's 130. Leave-one-meeting-out on the forced share is stable for SNX (0.387-0.446) and NOT stable for ADP (0.179-0.318); 23 of ADP's 24 not_supported insertions are in that one meeting and three of ADP's six meetings contribute zero forced-unmatched insertions. No single CELL dominates (largest 21.1% / 16.9% of insertions).

THE PRIMARY IS CONDITIONAL ON THE FROZEN MIDPOINT PUB-BOUNDARY RULE. midpoint gives 905 PUB tokens and 76/130 insertions; any_overlap 1052 and 50/95; wholly_contained 714 and 229/301 with forced shares that look far better. These are partly DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS, not error bars. Midpoint is primary because it is the shipped metric's rule - that chooses a primary, it does not establish robustness.

REGION CHANGES THE LEVEL. core_strict ADP 0.3120 rate / 0.527 forced and SNX 0.4123 / 0.689; core_envelope (primary) 0.0840 / 0.237 and 0.1436 / 0.408; clip 0.1095 / 0.383 and 0.1750 / 0.480. Three separate estimands, never summed or averaged, none estimating the others. This RECAPITULATES the parent study's region sensitivity; it does not confirm a common cause.

tau moves only the undecidable boundary: over {0.25,0.5,1.0} supported counts are 24/24/26 and 77/77/77 while undecidable grows 20/28/34 and 13/16/29 at the expense of not_supported. The undecidable class measures ASCERTAINABILITY under timestamp geometry and annotation coverage, not semantic doubt, and not_supported should be read as 'at most this many'.

ADP's undecidable share is three times SNX's (0.368 vs 0.123) and THE CAUSE IS NOT IDENTIFIED. The clock-artefact reading is not supported: the fraction of ALL region tokens whose dilated window lies wholly inside certain coverage is 0.695 [0.635,0.752] for ADP against 0.721 [0.669,0.774] for SNX. It is a property of the scoring pipeline and is NOT evidence that ADP is less reliable.

Alignment tie-break envelope over 6 op priorities x forward/reversed, applied to alignments A and B only (alignment C is computed over ALL minimum-cost paths and is tie-break-invariant by construction, reached by the envelope only through which tokens A labels I): ADP supported 0.303-0.346 and forced 0.185-0.259; SNX 0.561-0.611 and 0.408-0.443. This is an alignment SENSITIVITY envelope and must not be confused with the forced/possible identification band, which is computed over all minimum-cost alignment-C paths and holds the local assignment fixed.

The direct overlap test's interval is a TWO-cluster bootstrap: only 2 of the 6 meetings contribute any overlap-touching gold block (samothraki 18/37, xylokastro 7/37), so [0.189,0.486] is just the two per-meeting values. Read it as 'two meetings, both above the non-overlap rate', not as an interval.

The support matching maximises cardinality, so the supported COUNT does not depend on processing order; WHICH of two equally admissible gold occurrences a token receives still can, and that residual is outside the forced/possible band.
Cell selection is stream-stratified and deliberately OVERLAP-ENRICHED (P=11, I=4, H=4, M=3, R=4) and is not error-driven. Every pooled number is conditional on that mix and is not a natural rate.

Cross-system corroboration is ENRICHMENT evidence, not independent confirmation: ADP and SNX are both large speech models on overlapping web-scale material and correlated errors are exactly what it cannot rule out. n=25 for one direction.
The parent study's 80.3% is the MIRROR question (occurrences PUB has and ADP lacks - adapter deletions), not a second measurement of this one.

Two Codex reviews shaped this. Job 847c449f ran on the written design before any number existed and forced the asymmetric undecidability rule, the injective local matching as primary, alignment C, the not_said -> not_supported rename, global gold capacity, the strict-intersection overlap definition and the refusal of transport. Job cea10e78 ran on the findings before any claim was written and found a RATE-DENOMINATOR ERROR - cells with zero published tokens were being dropped, deflating numerator and rate in a self-flattering direction (69/905 reported for a system with 76 insertions) - and demanded maximum-cardinality matching, the forced/possible band, the omission_attributable rename, and the gold-denominator overlap test.
Zero GPU, zero paid API, no new audio, no confirmation spent. Aggregates only: eval/results_insertion_fidelity.json contains no transcript text.

experiments.title: Is the autoresearch confirmation partition still confirmatory for the LLM-composer family F1?
experiments.question: The LLM-composer plan's one surviving family (F1, override a wrong 2-of-3 majority) was selected by reading benchmark-wide oracle disagreements, error taxonomies and bucket sizes. Did any of those calculations include the four sealed confirmation cities, and if so may F1 still report a confirmatory CI?
experiments.conclusion: NO. VERDICT (b): CONFIRM IS INVALID AS CONFIRMATION FOR F1. Precisely - not universally poisoned, but unusable for this hypothesis, because F1's design decisions are traceable to specific reference-conditioned numbers computed with confirmation labels in the denominator. (1) The oracle counts and the majority-error taxonomy DID include the confirmation cities: column_census.py:38, exp_majority_taxonomy.py:365, exp_char_homophone.py:169 and exp_composition.py:295 all run on the bare fusion_lab.load_substrate(), whose only filter (fusion_lab.py:128-138) is the 6 sealed eval-freeze windows - there is no city filter, and all four result JSONs carry the header n_windows 247 / n_cities 10 / ref_tokens 74917. The 6,645 exact_2_of_3 columns, the 1,245 W-differs-from-oracle columns, the 1,719 wrong majorities, the linguistic buckets (function words 19.9%, entities 6.4%), the 41.8% zero-marginal-value figure and the '25.0% of the gap' figure that makes F1 exist at all are therefore all computed over 27,665 confirmation tokens as well as 47,252 search tokens. exp_majority_taxonomy.py:13 asserts 'the autoresearch confirmation partition is untouched'; that is true of the harness API and FALSE of the labels, and the same wrong claim sits in the taxonomy report (:9-10) and in that record's caveats. (2) Earlier CLOSED experiments quoted per-city outcomes over all 10 cities as a habit: composition-over-selection (LOO over cities, zero sign flips, 208/247 windows), name-repair-on-w ('9 of 10 cities negative', zero of 247 windows changed in D or I), char-vote-homophones ('5 cities better / 4 worse', 10 leave-one-city-out folds), roster-grounded-selection (no city carries it, 247 windows), fusion-deletions (247 windows). This is the seventh pass over the same substrate. (3) Term-list construction is a SEPARATE, NARROWER channel: the v1 base files are externally sourced ('OpenCouncil public city registry. No transcript text, no provider hypothesis.') but roster_lexicon.py:12-14 merges an admitted slice of the 147 error-mined candidates of exp-2026-08-16-error-mined-terms, mined from the human-correction corpus that overlaps this benchmark, of which 38 route to confirmation cities (sparta 15, xylokastro 10, samothraki 7, argos 6); and argos.v2.json rule_a rejects aliases by their frequency in the 220 benchmark windows of the eight non-argos/orestiada cities, three of which are confirmation cities. The source reports call the lists 'optimistic and leaky'. This contaminates any NAME or ENTITY number on confirm, in the optimistic direction; it does not independently contaminate a function-word arm that neither uses nor was designed from the lists. (4) THE ONE CLEAN ANSWER: the split is by CITY (autoresearch.py:102-103, _restrict at :203), strictly coarser than meeting, so no meeting and no window straddles; plan_partition (:131) reads only reference-token counts and assert_partition (:153) pins it. (5) The harness itself genuinely never read confirm: journal.jsonl holds 33 records - 16 REGISTERED, 16 SEARCH_RESULT, 1 DUPLICATE_REFUSED, ZERO CONFIRM_BATCH_FROZEN, ZERO CONFIRM_RESULT - and all 16 search results carry partition=search, n_windows=153, n_meetings=103. The 11-vs-16 discrepancy against the harness record is the five overlap-speaker arms appended later at git_head 437993d9; all five ran on 153 windows and none touched confirm. So 'never read' is true of the harness and false of analyst knowledge. OPTION (c) IS REFUSED: all 247 windows have been through at least six reference-conditioned passes, so carving from them restores no information independence, and the only genuinely unread material is the 7 sealed eval-freeze temporal-holdout windows at 2,101 reference tokens (2.8% of the substrate), where the -0.0010 ship floor is 2.1 edits against the 75 edits it is on the full substrate - underpowered by a factor of ~36, and sealed by a hard rule no arm has passed a gate to release. SECONDARY QUESTION SETTLED: the harness permits EXACTLY ONE frozen confirmation batch per PROTOCOL_VERSION (freeze_confirmation_batch raises if any CONFIRM_BATCH_FROZEN record exists, autoresearch.py:819-825) containing AT MOST 5 ideas (CONFIRM_BUDGET=5, :112, checked at :839). 'A budget of 5' in the harness report (:10) means five ideas inside the one batch; the same report says so at :67-73. The five-sequential-batches / 22.6% familywise scenario is exactly what the code forbids, so there is no conflict between code and report - only an ambiguous one-line denominator.
experiments.decision: F1 may be built and run, but reports EXPLORATORY results only: any interval is labelled descriptive, never confirmatory, never gate-valid, never multiplicity-controlled, and F1 may not be described as having passed the ship gate whatever it measures. NO confirmation batch is frozen and NO confirmation is spent - the budget stays 5 of 5 and the single available batch stays available. Any entity or name number from F1 carries the term-list leak caveat in the same sentence. The strongest honest claim available is 'on this fixed, previously analysed benchmark, a frozen F1 produced an exploratory dWER of X, with meeting and city heterogeneity Y'. If F1 runs at all, run it as a prospective-design exercise: freeze composer, prompt, thresholds, abstention policy and analysis before evaluating; ablate the leaky term resources out; report abstentions, failures, net edits and per-city heterogeneity; use the output for effect-size and power planning against a future sealed set, not as a ship decision. Three places carrying the now-corrected claim that the confirmation partition was untouched are named in the report and must be read against it: exp_majority_taxonomy.py:13, docs/reports/2026-08-17-majority-error-taxonomy.md:9-10, and the caveats of exp-2026-08-17-majority-error-taxonomy.
caveats: This is a forensic audit of provenance, not a measurement. Zero GPU, zero paid API, zero LLM calls on the substrate, no new number about any model.
It shows nothing about whether any confirmation RESULT is wrong: no confirmation result exists.
It does not show the harness is broken. The harness did what it was built to do; the leak is upstream of it, in analysis scripts that never called it and were never obliged to.

'CONFIRM is invalid as confirmation for F1' is deliberately narrower than 'the partition is contaminated'. A genuinely independent, previously unspecified hypothesis whose design demonstrably did not depend on the prior analyses could in principle still use the partition - but demonstrating that now would be hard, and F1 is not such a hypothesis (Codex 6eefa29e, point D).

The mere existence of earlier all-10-city records does not automatically contaminate every future hypothesis. It contaminates F1 because F1's specific design decisions are traceable to specific numbers in them.

The term-list finding is PARTLY yes, not yes: the v1 base lists are externally sourced and explicitly exclude transcript-derived terms. Only the error-mined slice (38 candidates routed to confirm cities) and one frequency stoplist rule touch benchmark material. rule_a rejected exactly 1 alias at its frozen threshold.
Agreement-with-OpenCouncil throughout. Every figure cited is an agreement number; nothing here says anything about fidelity-to-audio.

Reviewed by Codex job 6eefa29e (sol, high effort), which confirmed verdict (b), confirmed the confirmation-budget reading, separated the term-list channel as resource contamination distinct from hypothesis-selection contamination, and supplied the narrowing in caveat 4.

experiments.title: Does Soniox per-word confidence predict human-verified errors?
experiments.question: Soniox returns a per-word confidence our client throws away. Does it predict the errors a human listener actually found, well enough to justify one paid stt-async-v5 re-run over the 247 benchmark windows?
experiments.conclusion: YES on the FREE realtime model, and the decision is GO for one ~$0.82 paid run AS A HYPOTHESIS TEST, not as a validated capability. PRIMARY, frozen with its threshold before any outcome was computed: the equal-weight mean of the six WITHIN-MEETING AUROCs of 1-min-confidence for predicting that an EMITTED Soniox word is an error is 0.8167 (GO threshold 0.60, AUROC null 0.5), meeting-cluster 95% [0.790, 0.852] over 6 clusters (descriptive, not significance). All six meetings 0.782-0.900; leave-one-meeting-out 0.800-0.824; within-meeting permutation null (2000 perms) mean 0.4986, 95% [0.403, 0.602], observed outside the whole band, one-sided p=0.0005. Pooled AUROC 0.8185, average precision 0.453 against a prevalence null of 0.1453 on n=1005 emitted words / 146 errors. Bottom confidence decile: 0.510 error rate, 3.51x lift. | THE CEILING IS PART OF THE RESULT: in core_envelope M=859 S=97 D=43 I=49, so DELETIONS ARE 22.8% OF ALL EDIT OPERATIONS AND ARE INVISIBLE to a per-word confidence by construction. Every AUROC here is about substitutions and insertions among EMITTED words, never about all the errors the human found. Insertion detection is the WEAKEST of the three (mean WM 0.773, AP 0.226) and insertions are exactly what fails the occupancy gate in exp-2026-08-16-char-vote-homophones. | REPRODUCTION, the check that decided how much the rest was worth: pooled WER(cached, new) = 0.0216 over 27 cells (97.8% word agreement), but only 14/27 cells token-identical and 12/27 raw-identical. Realtime Soniox is not deterministic; word-level reproduction is strong, so the confidences attach to THIS re-run but not retroactively to the cached hyp/soniox text token by token. | FIRST CALIBRATION OF THE PRODUCTION THRESHOLD: the user's soniox-core flags min-lexical-rune confidence < 0.5, a UX judgement unchanged since 2026-06-14 and never checked against ground truth. Here it flags 3.4% of words at precision 0.706 / recall 0.164 / lift 4.86x - a high-specificity triage rule, not broad error detection. Calibration is broadly ordered but NOT strictly monotone ([0.8,0.9) sits 5.1 points above [0.7,0.8), SE ~8.5, noise-compatible) and NO calibrated error probability is claimed: 738 of 1005 words sit in one wide bucket. | TOOLING: soniox-tools gained a strictly additive on_token callback and a --json mode preserving text/confidence/start_ms/end_ms/is_final; stdout without --json is byte-identical, so every existing caller still works.
experiments.decision: GO for ONE paid stt-async-v5 run over the 247 windows (~8 audio hours, ~$0.82) to test whether the discrimination transports. Do NOT build a fusion arm on confidence before that run returns. Do NOT quote 0.8167 as coverage of ASR error - it is conditional on the word being emitted and 22.8% of edits are deletions it cannot see. Do NOT quote it as evidence about stt-async-v5. Keep the 247 windows on stt-async-v5: re-running them on rt-v4 would change one third of W and invalidate every frozen number. Silence trimming (soniox-core ?trim=1) stays OFF - it loses ~11% of words, this project's exact failure mode.
experiments.next_action: Superseded as a plan by exp-2026-08-16-w-rt-confidence, which ran the FREE stt-rt-v4 path over all 247 windows instead and found no confidence arm meeting its criteria. The ~$0.82 stt-async-v5 run is NOT justified by the fusion-arm hypothesis any more; it would need a different question.
caveats: 30 cells, 27 scored, 6 meetings, 6 cities, ONE MEETING PER CITY so meeting and city are fully confounded. The cell is the independent unit and clustering is by meeting. This CANNOT support a population claim or any promotion gate; a 6-cluster interval excluding a null is not significance.
stt-rt-v4 IS NOT stt-async-v5. Everything here is indirect evidence motivating an experiment, never evidence about the paid model's confidence.

The AUROC is conditional on the word being EMITTED. Deletions (22.8% of edits in the primary region, 31.2% in core_strict) are invisible to this rule. That is a limit of this rule, not a proof that deletions are undetectable - a neighbouring-word signal is conceivable and untested.

NOTHING WAS TUNED ON THE GOLD SET. Primary statistic, GO threshold 0.60, region, bucket edges, alignment tie-break and all nulls were written into the scorer docstring before the first metric ran. conf_min (min over ALL runes) is the preregistered aggregate; conf_min_lex (min over LEXICAL runes, the production definition) was added AFTER freezing once soniox-core's algorithm became known, and is reported alongside rather than substituted.

The overlap / insertion / substitution / region / alignment / subtoken analyses are SENSITIVITY CHECKS on one dataset varying one choice at a time. They are not independent replications. zografou jun18 contributes a single error and its 0.900 means almost nothing.
One meeting (samothraki jul6) supplies 69 of 146 errors (47%). Checked: its own AUROC is 0.783, at the low end, and excluding it the mean is 0.823. The headline is not one meeting's effect.

min-over-runes is mildly length-confounded (subtoken count alone predicts error at AUROC 0.555). Within fixed subtoken counts 1-6 the AUROCs are 0.79/0.81/0.86/0.88/0.85/0.78, so the signal survives the control; counts >=7 have n<=22 and are uninformative.
The 93.2% run-to-run word similarity from the user's soniox-core is a SEPARATE repeatability estimate (different metric, audio and client configuration), not a ceiling this run was scored against.

The 'maxJobs = 18 parallel sessions, so 8 audio hours is ~27 min wall clock' logistics note comes from soniox-core and was NOT verified here; it traces to an initial commit with no surviving measurement artefact.
soniox-tools at /home/harold/projects/soniox-tools is NOT a git repository, so the tooling change has no commit or revision to cite.

Every gold-set caveat still applies: one listener, one pass, no inter-annotator number, 19% of core tokens excluded as text-uncertain with their time masked out, and a reference that knowingly under-covers.

Two Codex reviews at high effort, each before the thing it governed. Job 4759402624f643efacc4fb2e9cd63beb ran BEFORE any scoring code and replaced a pooled AUROC with the within-meeting mean, corrected the null from 0 to 0.5, forced the deletion ceiling up front, required a within-meeting rather than global permutation null, and required the alignment envelope and length control. Job 69c1a01b05a54aa08deb776df756af8a ran on the findings BEFORE any claim was written and killed three sentences: 'nothing here is evidence about async-v5', 'robust across all six meetings', and 93.2% framed as a reproduction ceiling.
ZERO GPU, ZERO PAID API. Free Perplexity temp key on the realtime path, local CPU. The ~$0.82 is the proposed next step, not spend incurred.

2026-08-16, same day: the paid run this record recommended was NOT bought. exp-2026-08-16-w-rt-confidence instead rebuilt the whole substrate on the free stt-rt-v4 path (W-rt) and measured the fusion arms there. All three confirmatory arms failed, and the post-hoc diagnostic put confidence's AUROC at 0.587-0.703 on the decisions a fusion arm actually makes, against the 0.8167 in this record. Read that report before quoting 0.8167 as if it were available to a fusion arm.

experiments.title: The corrected adapter on the OpenCouncil benchmark
experiments.question: Does the corrected (post-label-prefix-fix) adapter beat base whisper and the commercial providers on the 260-window benchmark?
experiments.conclusion: On the 40 training-disjoint windows (argos+orestiada, 12,194 words) the corrected adapter scores 0.1548 wer-nofillers: statistically indistinguishable from Scribe v2 (+1.14, 90% [-0.58, +2.79]) and Soniox (+1.26, [-0.33, +2.80]), and better than base whisper (-2.30, [-4.02, -0.77]) and than its own broken predecessor (-1.77, [-2.66, -0.98]). 260/260 items, 0 errors, $0.30.
experiments.decision: The label-prefix fix bought a real 1.77 points on unseen cities, sign consistent (26 windows better / 11 worse / 3 tied). Publish the corrected adapter. Do not read the base comparison as a weights effect - it is cross-stack.
caveats: 7 of the 260 windows are meetings dated >= 2026-06-01, inside the temporal TEST definition; one of them (win_argos_jun3_2026_855222) supplied 21% of the base comparison. Re-measured on the 39 clean validation windows every conclusion survives: ours 0.1542, vs base -1.87 [-3.35,-0.50], vs broken -1.58 [-2.41,-0.85], vs Scribe +1.12 [-0.54,+2.73], vs Soniox +1.19 [-0.48,+2.70]. Exclude those 7 from any future final measurement.
argos+orestiada is part of the VALIDATION set, not the test set, and has been scored repeatedly and used to decide which experiments to stop. Treat the number as potentially optimistically biased.
The base-whisper arm runs on the HuggingFace serverless pipeline, a different decoder stack. The -2.30 includes an engine difference.
The broken-adapter arm ran on an RTX 3090 in July, ours on an RTX A4000 today. Measured separately: CPU int8 and CUDA int8 give different tokens from the same artifact, so the device is not neutral.
The reference is OpenCouncil's own published text, so this measures agreement-with-OpenCouncil, not accuracy.
One seed. The mixture experiment measured 2.1 points of per-seed spread, larger than the 1.77 claimed here.

experiments.title: Full LoRA training run
experiments.question: Does the full training recipe produce a usable adapter?
experiments.conclusion: Reported gains were measured against unfairly-served baselines, and the run carried the label-prefix bug.
experiments.decision: Do not migrate or cite. Retrained as exp-2026-08-02-fulltrain-corrected.

experiments.title: Contextual biasing with roster hotwords
experiments.question: Can inference-time biasing get the name accuracy the fine-tune was supposed to buy?
experiments.conclusion: Measured properly on the corrected adapter (artifact-ct2-fixed, 39 frozen validation windows, CPU int8, preregistered hash-ordered 160-token surname hotwords, meeting-clustered bootstrap): biasing does lift names - mention recall 51.2%->65.4%, precision 93.3%->96.4%, substitutions -82 with CI excluding zero - but it CAUSES deletions: +133 (del_rate +0.0112 [+0.0020,+0.0207], CI excludes zero). Net WER +0.34 points [-0.61,+1.31]; fails the preregistered non-inferiority gate (upper bound +0.0131 vs margin +0.0010). The mechanism is prompt-induced skipping: hotwords share the 448-token decoder context. The 2026-07-25 name-subset signal is confirmed directionally, but the WER cost lands on the deletion side, our worst error class.
experiments.decision: Do not ship decode-time hotword biasing. The post-hoc roster repair arm of exp-2026-08-11-name-repair delivers name correction (-30 subs, -0.25 WER, CI excludes zero, zero collateral) with no decode cost and no deletion penalty; name work continues there. The preregistered exploratory 200-token secondary was NOT run: the failure mechanism (longer prompt -> more skipping) predicts it is worse, and the primary already failed its gate.
caveats: Stack: CPU int8, beam=5, faster-whisper `hotwords` param (not initial_prompt). The mini-PC serves beam=2 on GPU; magnitudes do not transfer unchecked, but the deletion mechanism is decoder-context arithmetic and should.
160-token budget holds ~20 of 32-36 roster surnames per meeting (hash-decorrelated exclusions); full coverage is impossible under faster-whisper's 223-token hotword cap.
Raw results: ~/.cache/oc-public/serving-stack/results-B-eval.json (eval-B-hotwords.json hypotheses). Harness scripts/serving_stack/hotwords_arm.py, 26 tests.

experiments.question: Is the correction dataset a lexical signal wearing an acoustic costume?
experiments.conclusion: Supported. The LLM post-editor reached 0.155 -> 0.119 WER on 50 corrected utterances, better than fine-tuning.

experiments.question: What has been tried, on what data, with what result - as one document?
experiments.conclusion: Dataset: 22.47h train (11.16h human corrections + 11.32h unverified no_edit labels), 2.79s mean clip, 209 meetings, 9 cities, Aug 2024 - May 2026. Ten adapters trained. Only the label-prefix fix produced a measured gain.
experiments.decision: Use this as the input document when designing the next training run.

experiments.title: Where the gap to Scribe actually is
experiments.question: What kinds of errors separate our adapter from Scribe v2, and which are worth attacking?
experiments.conclusion: The 1.12-point gap is concentrated, not diffuse: the 8 worst windows account for 193 errors while the total gap is 133, so we are ahead in aggregate on the other 31. Four patterns: 2 decoder-degeneration windows, 2 name-dense windows (roll call, agenda), lost short speaker turns, and number/protocol formatting. 21.6% of our substitution errors are person or place names, almost all off by 1-2 characters. Style conventions favour US, not Scribe, so the true acoustic gap is larger than 1.12. Taxonomy pass: our deficit is +3.49 pts in real recognition categories, offset by -2.51 in convention categories (of which -2.27 is number formatting and insertions). Neutralise the convention and the true acoustic gap is ~3.5 points, not 1.0. Deletion-to-insertion ratio 3.3:1 vs Scribe's 1.6:1.
experiments.decision: Do not retrain to close this gap. A per-meeting name lexicon (~0.4-0.6 pts) plus anti-hallucination decoding config (~0.5 pts) attack ~0.9-1.1 of the 1.12 points with no training. Diacritics, generic spell post-editing and reference-style mimicry are dead ends.
caveats: Per-window we lose on 24 and win on 12; the aggregate favours us on the non-worst windows only because our wins are larger. Not 'broadly better with exceptions'.
The a/b/c split (60-65% genuine / 15-20% style / 15-20% bad reference) is a qualitative estimate from 8 windows, not a measurement.

experiments.title: Post-hoc name repair and decoder ablations
experiments.question: Can a roster-based name lexicon and anti-degeneration decoding close the gap without retraining, net positive?
experiments.conclusion: Arm E survives the substrate change and stays the project's one measured positive, but it is small and it is not shippable as written. Re-measured on W (per-column composition) after V was displaced: W 0.10046 -> W+E 0.09971, dWER -0.00075 [-0.00109,-0.00044], preregistered DIRECTIONAL primary endpoint met (CI upper bound below zero), both rate gates pass, and the raw counts show why - S 3200 -> 3144 while D 1522 -> 1522 and I 2804 -> 2804, unchanged not only pooled but in ZERO of 247 windows. 36 windows better / 205 tied / 6 worse; LOO over windows, meetings and cities gives no sign flip; 9 of 10 cities negative. 97 firings in 52 windows / 44 meetings, 86 at distance 1. No single-item domination: 56 net reference edits removed, largest window AND largest meeting 5 = 8.9%, 33 meetings improve / 5 worsen. Recovers 1.4% of the W-to-column-oracle gap. THE DESIGN QUESTION WAS THE JOB. E's rule 'act only where the three systems disagree' was a token-SET rule, well defined only for whole-window selection. Re-specified positionally and frozen before any number: a W token inherits its MSA column and is protected iff that column is class `agree`. Codex job 73670922 confirmed this is the correct occurrence-level port and that it is strictly LESS protective than the set rule, with no reverse case. The choice not to protect `exact_2_of_3` in the primary arm (that class is settled for the ARBITRATION arms H/C, which swap in the dissenting system's candidate; E does neither) was preregistered with the stricter reading as a declared secondary. Both arms pass. The direct paired contrasts settle the ordering: W+E-unrestricted minus W+E = +0.00044 [+0.00020,+0.00069] and W+E-strict minus W+E = +0.00032 [+0.00013,+0.00053], both excluding zero. Firing on unanimous columns is net harmful (24 windows worse, CI includes zero, gates FAIL); protecting token majorities throws away real gain. THE COVERAGE CLAIM THAT WOULD HAVE KILLED THE ARM IS WRONG. The 2026-08-17 untried-inventory's '56 of 260 windows (21.5%) have a roster' does not replicate: actual coverage is 238/260 windows (91.5%) and 183/203 meetings (90.1%); on the substrate 232/247 (93.9%) and 133/144 meetings. 56 is the fetch-FAILURE count in data/pii/fetch_rosters.log. E is a no-op on 6% of the benchmark, not 78.5%. The 15 no-roster windows are byte-exact no-ops (delta 0.00000, 15/15 tied). What survives from the audit: all 7 sealed temporal-holdout meetings do have zero-length rosters, which is the real and narrower reason E fired zero times there. THE BHMA-3 GATES CANNOT BE JUDGED. Four of six (beneficial-change precision, harmful-change bound, no wrong-person substitution, beneficial-minus-5x-harmful) need per-change adjudication against a name ground truth that exists only for the Step-0 audit sample, never for W. Gate 3 ('zero correct->wrong across >=300 activatable points on untouched meetings') is UNASSESSABLE on the current holdout: rosters do not exist there, and the measured supply is 150 firings / 179 candidate-stage points over 76,199 W tokens, i.e. 0.61-0.72 per two-minute window, so 300 points needs ~390-465 roster-covered windows (13-15 h) of audio this project has never scored. Only gate 5 is numerically met, and on development data. The plan's own clause governs: not enough activations means shadow/suggestion mode, not automatic shipping.
experiments.decision: CLOSE with a positive that ships to SHADOW ONLY. E stays the cheap post-hoc step after W, wired behind the Bhma-3 shadow gates, and no automatic deployment follows from this number. Do not re-open the arm on this substrate: three protection policies were preregistered and all three are reported, and a fourth would be variant hunting on the fifth pass over the same 247 windows. What would change the answer is not another arm - it is (a) untouched, roster-covered audio, and (b) a name-level human adjudication of E's own firings, which is what gates 1-4 have always required and this project has never produced for W. The pending v2 alias fix for the two registry-vs-reference orthography conflicts (Adrachtas/Kadolou) is confirmed STILL PENDING: neither the v1 nor the v2 term files carry those aliases. It is a lexicon change, not a blocker on this measurement, which used the frozen v1 files unchanged from the V-era run.
caveats: Codex review: the decoder work is NOT one config - no_speech_threshold deletes speech, temperature fallback generates new garbage, overlap merge duplicates words. Separate ablations, and it does not go first.
The right comparison is paired against our own current system on identical weights, not against Scribe. Seed variance then does not enter.

experiments.title: Decode thresholds against the deletion rate
experiments.question: Does moving one of the faster-whisper decode thresholds the server leaves at default lower our deletion rate without costing WER?
experiments.conclusion: No. Six preregistered arms on the 39 frozen windows collapse into TWO distinct decode behaviours. The no-speech gate fired ZERO times across all 39 windows, so arms B (no_speech_threshold=0.8) and C (None, primary) are byte-identical to the control and could not have changed a token; arm E (log_prob_threshold=None) is identical too, because its fallback trigger fired only twice and both times on segments the compression threshold had already sent to fallback. Arms D (temperature=[0.0], primary) and F (compression_ratio_threshold=None) are identical to each other and differ from the control on 3 of 39 windows: micro-WER +0.00042 [-0.00460,+0.00492], deletion rate +0.00235 [-0.00100,+0.00773], insertion rate +0.00025 [-0.00057,+0.00124]. All three point estimates are WORSE and all three intervals cross zero. No arm passes its gate. Control: WER 0.1589, deletions 0.0600, insertions 0.0201, 715 D to 240 I.
experiments.decision: The served decode configuration stays as it is. The finding that matters is mechanistic, not statistical: our deletions are not produced by segment skipping (the gate never fires) and not by the temperature fallback (removing it increases them). The 'deletions are the cheap half' direction from exp-2026-08-11-wer-levers-research does not survive at the decode-config level. The 7 temporal holdout windows were NOT decoded and remain sealed, because the prereg only releases them to confirm an arm that passed.

experiments.title: Final report: does domain fine-tuning of whisper-large-v3 pay for Greek council transcription?

experiments.title: Targeted retraining against within-span deletions
experiments.question: Does a deletion-targeted training mix (55% expanded clean backbone / 25% verified deletion-coverage hard examples / 10% names / 10% other), 3 seeds per arm vs an expanded-pool neutral control, lower the deletion rate without raising insertions or WER?
experiments.conclusion: SCREEN RESULT 2026-08-16 (single seed 101; measured per-seed spread is 2.1 WER points, so this decides nothing alone). Both screens were merged, converted to CT2 int8 and decoded on the LOCAL minipc stack only (CPU, 16 threads, frozen control decode config, common random numbers, same normalizer); four distinct model.bin sha256 (control 8a1a3b25, RUN1 d808868a, RUN2-stage1 96088a40, RUN2-stage2 444de4e9). 39 frozen windows / 31 meetings / 11,911 ref tokens; paired bootstrap over meetings, 4000 replicates. control WER 0.1589 del 0.0600 ins 0.0201 sub 0.0788 | RUN1 WER 0.1641 del 0.0788 ins 0.0174 sub 0.0680 | RUN2-stage2 WER 0.1591 del 0.0756 ins 0.0163 sub 0.0672. vs control both arms: WER delta includes zero (+0.0052 / +0.0002), del_rate RISES with CI excluding zero (+0.0187 [+0.0012,+0.0414] / +0.0155 [+0.0016,+0.0341]), sub_rate FALLS with CI excluding zero (-0.0107 / -0.0115), ins_rate falls but includes zero. Leave-one-window-out does not reverse any del/sub/ins sign; the RUN2 WER delta's sign flips on 13 of 39 windows and is read as flat, never as better. DS-WER v2 entities (primary, 274 occurrences, never decides alone): control 0.5365, RUN1 0.6058, RUN2 0.5657; the same S->D swap appears there (entities S/D 114/26 -> 70/93 -> 90/58). v1: 0.512 / 0.596 / 0.536. READING: both stage-2-containing screens traded substitutions for deletions - the mix built to REDUCE deletions is followed by MORE deletions in both arms, with WER flat, which a pooled-WER-only look would have missed entirely. Neither arm meets the frozen primary criterion (deletion drop without insertion/WER regression), so the control artifact-adapter-fixed keeps the candidate slot. Pipeline-bug check done first and clean: distinct fingerprints, stage2.log records LoRA initialized from trained stage-1 weights (192 nonzero lora_B), identical stage-2 substrate (n_train 42,204 / max_steps 10,552 in both runs), S+D+I reproduce the WERs, no arm near the +2-point bug threshold. FOR THIS RECORD: RUN1 IS this mix's screen, and the mixture it actually trained on is NOT the 55/25/10/10 of the question above: the realized exposure over 42,204 presentations was 68.9/18.6/2.6/10.0 (backbone/deletion-hard/names/other). 55/25/10/10 is the PLANNED mix; every result below belongs to the executed 68.9/18.6/2.6/10.0 one, and the gap (a smaller deletion-hard and a much smaller names share than designed) is itself a candidate explanation for the outcome. It did not lower the deletion rate; it raised it (+0.0187 per ref token, CI excludes zero, 715 -> 938 deletions) while lowering substitutions (938 -> 810) and leaving WER statistically flat. The stated goal of the mix is therefore not achieved on one seed, in the direction opposite to the hypothesis. Association, not proof of cause: one seed per arm, no ablation separating data composition from anything else in the run, and aggregate counts do not show that particular substitutions became deletions.
experiments.decision: Close this training question for the current cycle. Neither single-seed screen lowered deletions; both raised them with intervals excluding zero, and the follow-up deletion-hard coverage audit established neither frozen reopening gate. Keep artifact-adapter-fixed in the candidate slot. Do not spend GPU or run a blind confirmation without a new reason and the preregistered three-seed matched-GPU design.

experiments.title: HParl audio-vs-text faithfulness probe and Soniox alignment filter
experiments.question: Are the HParl transcripts faithful to their own audio, and can a Soniox-alignment filter carve a usable training subset out of them?
experiments.conclusion: Usable audio, unusable targets. On 100 random utterances (16 speakers, shards test-00000 seed 20260814 n=40 and train-00023 seed 7 n=60) verified against Soniox: rows without a [UNK] placeholder disagree at 6.1% WER with a 1.9% deletion rate and a 53% exact-match rate - i.e. the feared editorial-rewrite defect is NOT present at segment level. What disqualifies the corpus is target format: 52-60% of rows in each of three shards read carry at least one [UNK] placeholder over real speech (drives the pooled 7.7% deletion rate), and ZERO rows in any shard carry an accent or punctuation mark - the references are lowercase, unaccented, unpunctuated, while our labels are accented, punctuated clean-verbatim. Segments are ~3s-boundary alignment windows (median 4.7s / 9 tokens), so words are chopped at the edges. Storage is not a constraint: 32 kbps mono MP3 is 4.1 kB/s, ~1.8 GB for the full ~120h. ADDENDUM same day: the ML-processed mirror Elormiden/Hellenic-greek-parliamentary-speech (92,133 clips, 13.8 GB) is the usable one - 99.9% of rows are ACCENTED and none carry [UNK], but 59% carry <spoken_noise> markers and 0% carry punctuation. Filter run (eval/hparl2_filter.py, 150 random rows of test-00000, seed 20260814, tags stripped, alignment = 1 - WER on greek_normalize tokens): pooled WER 0.093 (sub .047 / del .028 / ins .018); align>=0.95 keeps 49% of rows = 50% of audio (~60h of 120h), align>=0.90 keeps 59%, align>=0.80 keeps 81%. TWO CAVEATS ON THAT 60h: (a) median row is 9 reference tokens so >=0.95 is effectively an exact-match test - it selects easy audio and yields a Soniox-agreement sample, not a random one; (b) <spoken_noise> is NOT the discriminator, keep rate is 48% on tagged vs 52% on untagged rows. The lowercase/unpunctuated target problem survives the filter untouched. ddamianos/hparl local cache deleted 2026-08-14. PUNCTUATION STAGE 2026-08-14: eval/hparl2_punctuate.py builds the label as dataset-words + Soniox-punctuation. Deterministic transfer() marks 96% of the 74 kept rows but copies Soniox's terminal period onto fragments (64/74 end in a final mark). gpt-5.6-luna (via the codex bridge, batches of 25, low effort) was run under a HARD WORD GUARD - output is accepted only if its greek_normalize token sequence is identical to the dataset transcript: 74/74 passed, zero words changed. It differs from transfer() on 61/74 rows, and judges only 19/74 (26%) of segments to be COMPLETE SENTENCES, with terminal punctuation matching that judgement 19/19. Three quarters of this corpus's segments are fragments; a naive punctuation pass would teach a sentence end every ~5s. PILOT PASS LANDED 2026-08-14: 10,133 rows across all 28 shards. keep@0.95 = 46.3% (vs 49% on the 150-row sample), pooled WER 0.100 (sub .052 / del .030 / ins .017), 6.18h kept of 13.57h processed, per-shard keep rate 42-52% (median 46%) - extrapolates to ~55h of the 120h. CORRECTION: the earlier claim that <spoken_noise> is NOT a discriminator was an n=150 artifact. At n=10,133 tagged rows keep 40.8% vs untagged 54.1%. The tag is real signal (it marks audio the transcript does not spell out, and the ASR hears it), but it is not sufficient - 41% of tagged rows pass - so admission stays with the alignment score. HUMAN CALIBRATION LANDED 2026-08-14 (43 judged rows, exported from the review page, fetched from the laptop; the two review rounds separated by regenerating both page item lists from their seeds - 29 gate judgements, 13 punctuation judgements, 1 ambiguous and excluded). THE 0.95 GATE IS TOO STRICT: precision is perfect (6/6 kept rows accepted) but 57% of the rows it DROPPED were judged good. By band: align 1.00 100% good (n=6), 0.85-0.95 88% (n=8), 0.50-0.85 75% (n=8), <0.50 0% (n=7) - the cliff is at ~0.50, not 0.95. On the pilot that costs hours: 0.95 keeps 46% of rows / 6.18h, 0.90 keeps 61% / 8.81h, 0.85 keeps 72% / 10.50h (extrapolating 55h vs 78h vs 93h of the 120h). NOT ADOPTED: 6-8 rows per band is a signal, not a calibration, and the page shows the alignment score so the judgement was not blind. Punctuation round: 11/13 accepted (85%), both rejections at align 1.00 i.e. punctuation complaints not row-quality ones. PACK REBUILT 2026-08-14: 4,546 rows / 6.12 h, sha256(train.jsonl)=275516c4fd269af0, 26.2% complete sentences, 145 rows dropped for <3 tokens. Punctuation pass over all 4,693 kept rows: 4,663 LLM outputs accepted, 30 (0.6%) word-guard rejected and fell back to deterministic transfer; the LLM differs from transfer on 88% of rows. BLIND CALIBRATION LANDED 2026-08-14, 62/62 judged, and it overturns the gate. Good control (>0.99) passes 6/6 yes. Band 0.80-0.95: 25/25 yes. Band 0.50-0.80: 22 yes / 3 idk / 0 no. BAD CONTROL (<0.40) FAILS: 3 yes / 1 idk / 2 no - half the rows scored below 0.40 do say their text. They are 1-2s clips where Soniox returned something unrelated, so a low alignment score mostly means SONIOX FAILED, not that the label is wrong: the gate has been measuring ASR confidence and charging the corpus for it. Against the 62 judgements: align>=0.95 admits 6 and throws away 50 good rows; >=0.85 admits 26, throws away 30; >=0.50 admits 56 with ZERO bad rows and throws away 3; >=0.50 + dur>=1.5s admits 53 (51 yes / 2 idk / 0 no) and throws away 5. Both 'no' rows are align 0.00 AND under 1.5s, so a duration floor removes the failure mode. The 4 'don't know' rows are boundary clipping ('the start was cut, I heard half the first word') and ALL FOUR carry a missing first/last reference token - but those flags also fire on 28 human-approved rows, so edge flags are a DOWN-WEIGHTING signal, not an admission rule. Pilot yield: >=0.50 + dur>=1.5s keeps 93% of rows / 13.22h of 13.57h, extrapolating ~117h of the 120h vs 55h at the current gate. hparl2-v2 BUILT 2026-08-14 at the preregistered gate: 9,334 rows / 13.16 h (11.66 h weighted), sha256=29f4fe806b88e80a, 24.2% edge-clipped at weight 0.5, 22.8% complete sentences; 439 rows dropped under 1.5s, 102 under 3 tokens. 2.2x the hours of v1 from the same pilot audio.
experiments.decision: Do not stage HParl as-is. experiments.title: External Greek corpora as stage-1 packs: STOMA, EuroSpeech-el, Common Voice Scripted 26.0
experiments.question: Do additional external Greek speech corpora, admitted through the pack pipeline and used as stage-1 adaptation before the frozen in-domain stage-2 recipe, lower agreement-WER on the 39 frozen validation windows without a deletion-rate regression?
experiments.conclusion: SCREEN RESULT 2026-08-16 (single seed 101; measured per-seed spread is 2.1 WER points, so this decides nothing alone). Both screens were merged, converted to CT2 int8 and decoded on the LOCAL minipc stack only (CPU, 16 threads, frozen control decode config, common random numbers, same normalizer); four distinct model.bin sha256 (control 8a1a3b25, RUN1 d808868a, RUN2-stage1 96088a40, RUN2-stage2 444de4e9). 39 frozen windows / 31 meetings / 11,911 ref tokens; paired bootstrap over meetings, 4000 replicates. control WER 0.1589 del 0.0600 ins 0.0201 sub 0.0788 | RUN1 WER 0.1641 del 0.0788 ins 0.0174 sub 0.0680 | RUN2-stage2 WER 0.1591 del 0.0756 ins 0.0163 sub 0.0672. vs control both arms: WER delta includes zero (+0.0052 / +0.0002), del_rate RISES with CI excluding zero (+0.0187 [+0.0012,+0.0414] / +0.0155 [+0.0016,+0.0341]), sub_rate FALLS with CI excluding zero (-0.0107 / -0.0115), ins_rate falls but includes zero. Leave-one-window-out does not reverse any del/sub/ins sign; the RUN2 WER delta's sign flips on 13 of 39 windows and is read as flat, never as better. DS-WER v2 entities (primary, 274 occurrences, never decides alone): control 0.5365, RUN1 0.6058, RUN2 0.5657; the same S->D swap appears there (entities S/D 114/26 -> 70/93 -> 90/58). v1: 0.512 / 0.596 / 0.536. READING: both stage-2-containing screens traded substitutions for deletions - the mix built to REDUCE deletions is followed by MORE deletions in both arms, with WER flat, which a pooled-WER-only look would have missed entirely. Neither arm meets the frozen primary criterion (deletion drop without insertion/WER regression), so the control artifact-adapter-fixed keeps the candidate slot. Pipeline-bug check done first and clean: distinct fingerprints, stage2.log records LoRA initialized from trained stage-1 weights (192 nonzero lora_B), identical stage-2 substrate (n_train 42,204 / max_steps 10,552 in both runs), S+D+I reproduce the WERs, no arm near the +2-point bug threshold. EXTERNAL-PACK VERDICT: RUN2 vs RUN1 paired on the same windows shows NO detected difference - every CI includes zero (WER -0.0050 [-0.0195,+0.0090], del -0.0032 [-0.0193,+0.0121], ins -0.0011, sub -0.0008; head2head 19/4/16; the del sign flips on one window). Per the frozen tree BOTH arms advance. 'Not detected' is not 'no effect': RUN2 bundles external stage-1 data + 5,190 extra optimizer updates + a different training GPU (A5000 vs A40), and this design cannot attribute anything among them; the CIs cover meeting-sampling uncertainty for fixed checkpoints, not training-seed uncertainty, which is larger than every delta here. The earlier prereg's point-estimate promotion rule (WER delta < 0 AND del delta <= 0 vs the baseline arm) is technically satisfied by RUN2 vs RUN1, which governs promotion relative to RUN1 only and says nothing about replacing the control. COST: RUN1 ~$6.20 (A40 t6ugwl9f4efu23) + RUN2 $6.74 (24.96h x $0.27, A5000 hwydnokhc60y2f) = ~$12.94 against the $22 ceiling; evaluation cost $0 on local CPU; zero pods alive.
experiments.decision: Close the external-pack screen for this cycle. The executed RUN2 recipe did not show a detectable improvement over RUN1, and both stage-2-containing arms raised deletions against the control. No confirmation round is authorised while the shared training freeze holds; any future confirmation needs three seeds and matched GPUs.
