experiments.conclusion: MECHANISM PILOT ONLY, 5 windows, 2026-08-20. The 39-window run was NOT performed (the user capped the work at the small test), so there are NO confirmatory numbers and no arm is adopted. | ALL THREE ARMS PASS THEIR MECHANISM CHECK. F: on the 5 pilot windows P's 7 forced cuts become 3 blind + 4 probability-valley cuts, with zero pieces under 5 s, zero over 29.5 s, exact integer-sample tiling, and every repaired cut inside a recorded valley of >=100 ms with mean speech probability <0.35. The mechanism fires but does not eliminate blind cuts: 3 of 7 seams had no qualifying valley in the 2 s slack. C: instrumented model.get_prompt confirms the prompt reaches the decoder on 31/31 pieces -- the first call of each piece k>=2 receives exactly the recorded 59-64 token ids preceded by sot_prev and followed by sot_sequence, and every later call receives []. Codex's warning was borne out: a <=29.5 s piece is NOT always one decoder iteration (several pieces made 2 get_prompt calls), so the original one-window justification was too strong; the oracle covers it. W: word ownership is an exact two-way partition -- 2,894 candidates, 1,511 kept, 1,381 non-owner, 2 outside audio, kept iff the emitting window owns the tile of the word's own midpoint. The residual risk is measured rather than assumed away: mean seam disagreement 12.97% of tokens in the +/-1 s band around a tile edge. | DESCRIPTIVE 5-WINDOW RATES (NOT INFERENTIAL, NOT A GATE, chosen because P cuts blind in them; N=1,625 reference tokens, 5 meetings): A WER 0.18831 / (S+D)/N 0.17908; P 0.18154 / 0.17108; F 0.17108 / 0.16123; C 0.17477 / 0.16431; W 0.17538 / 0.16677; E 0.33969 / 0.22646; E-WT 0.30338 / 0.20185. | THE ONE STRUCTURAL FINDING THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE SAMPLE SIZE: W - E-WT is -0.12800 on WER. Turning word timestamps on barely helped the old merge (E 0.33969 -> E-WT 0.30338); it is the WORD-LEVEL OWNERSHIP RULE, not the timestamps, that removes arm E's insertion catastrophe (insertion rate 0.11323 -> 0.10154 under the old merge, but 0.00862 under word ownership). That is exactly the confound E-WT was derived to expose, and it is answered. | REPRODUCIBILITY: the review fixes forced a full re-decode, and F, C and W each produced byte-identical text on all 5 windows across two independent runs. The arm C prompt-join defect CodeRabbit found was latent, not active: prompt token counts were unchanged (42-64 per piece). | ARM X (all three mechanisms in one decode, added on request and decoded on the same 5 windows) FAILS its mechanism check while posting the BEST WER of any arm here: WER 0.16062 and (S+D)/N 0.14585, against P's 0.18154 / 0.17108. The check that failed is F's: X takes 7 blind cuts on the pilot windows, exactly as many as P's 7 forced cuts, and the valley repair fired ONCE. The cause is structural, not a bug. X has to fit a core piece plus a 2 s margin on each side inside one 30 s Whisper window, so it cuts at 25.5 s instead of 29.5 s; the shorter ceiling manufactures new boundaries (7-8 pieces per window against F's 6-7) faster than the valley search repairs them, and it is worse per boundary too (21% blind vs F's 12.5%). The criterion was frozen before X was decoded and is not being relaxed to let the best number through.
experiments.decision: Nothing is adopted. Arm P remains the decoding candidate. F is the cleanest successor -- it is the only arm that removes blind cuts rather than working around them, it passed every mechanism check, and it changes P's behaviour only in the 14 windows where P cuts blind. X is the most interesting and the least understood: best WER, failed mechanism, and a known confound between its three ingredients. W is no longer refuted the way arm E was: word-level ownership is now known to be the missing ingredient. None of this can be settled on 5 windows chosen because P cuts blind in them.
experiments.next_action: Decode and score F, C, W and X on all 39 frozen windows (roughly 6 h local CPU; code and caches are in place: `eval/seam_repair.py decode --arm F|C|W|X` then `score`), so the arms sit in the same table as V, P and E. If X still leads there, the follow-up that separates its ingredients is an arm with X's 25.5 s ceiling and margin but WITHOUT the valley repair, which would price the margin on its own. Even the 39-window run stays exploratory -- these windows generated the forced-cut hypothesis -- so adoption needs the 247-window benchmark afterwards.
caveats: EXPLORATORY BY CONSTRUCTION. The 39 frozen windows generated the forced-cut hypothesis that arm F attacks, so re-running on them is not independent confirmation however many bootstrap replicates are used. The 5 pilot windows are worse: they were selected BECAUSE P cuts blind in them, so their rates are not a small version of the 39-window answer.
The 5-window intervals are quoted only to show their width. With 5 windows over 5 meetings and a meeting-clustered bootstrap, every arm's WER interval against control A spans zero.

F and C keep arm P's exact seeding (one ctranslate2.set_random_seed per window, before the piece loop) so they stay comparable to the cached P. With temperature fallback, arms with different piece counts consume different random streams, so 'common random numbers' is weaker than the phrase suggests.

Decoder nondeterminism was measured incidentally and is nil here: the CodeRabbit fixes forced a full re-decode, and all three arms produced byte-identical text on all 5 windows across two independent runs from fresh model processes. That is 5 windows on one machine, not a general determinism guarantee. The bootstrap still covers window/meeting sampling only.

KNOWN DEFECT, NOT FIXED HERE: chunking_decode.combine_piece_transcripts joins segment strings with no separator. Codex found that per-segment strip plus space-join changes tokenization in 7 of 39 windows on the cached P decode, recovering seven fused tokens. Fixing it would make every number incomparable with the published V/P/E table, so it is recorded as its own question. Arm W assembles from words instead; a test asserts a segment's words rejoin to that segment's own text under ftoks, so W is not advantaged by the difference.

W's word-level merge gives exactly one owner per CANDIDATE, not per spoken WORD. Two decodes of the same boundary word can land on opposite sides of a tile edge, producing a duplicate or a hole. Measured, not solved: 12.97% mean seam disagreement.
The freeze manifest holds 39 eval windows and 7 temporal-holdout windows; the project's 16 locked benchmark windows are a separate sealed set. Neither sealed set was touched.

Arm X's segmentation is NOT arm P's or F's: the 25.5 s ceiling it needs to fit its margins changes every boundary, so X is not a strict superset of F and no difference between them is attributable to the margin alone.

experiments.title: Does the clean-pack advantage survive six times more training
experiments.question: At 1,800 frozen steps instead of 300, does the overlap-free contiguous-pack arm still beat the incumbent short-clip arm on paired validation WER, and does the effect grow?
experiments.conclusion: SCREEN - STOP, and the effect did not grow - it dissolved. Six adapters, three paired seeds (13/29/47), 1,800 frozen steps, one GPU float16 stack, 39 validation windows. Mean delta WER -0.00252 (per seed -0.01108 / -0.00730 / +0.01083); all three meeting-clustered CIs cross zero and seed 47 reverses sign while worsening BOTH deletions (+0.00571) and insertions (+0.00563). Against the 300-step rung the point estimate shrank ~4x (-0.00982 -> -0.00252) while the across-seed standard deviation grew ~4x (0.00290 -> 0.01171); t(2) goes from -5.87 to -0.37 (post-hoc, not preregistered). Mechanism, measured: with effective batch 8 the two arms were never trained at comparable points on their curves. Arm A holds 28,967 rows and completed 0.08 epochs at 300 steps and 0.50 at 1,800 - it has never finished one epoch. Arm B holds 2,475 packs and completed 0.97 and 5.82. The crossing is the expected shape of arm B peaking near one pass and overfitting by six while arm A is still learning. The three arm-B runs ended at training losses 0.698/0.696/0.682, so no run is technically broken and the scatter is genuine generalization variance. Gate 6 fired at ~0.32 on all three seeds, but with a net effect of 0.0025 any window carries a large share: near zero net the domination gate measures effect size, not domination. Two previously unrecorded confounds are now quantified: arm A trains on a curated 'corrections + no-edit backbone' parquet while arm B has no correction enrichment at all - only 2.5% of pack utterances are corrections and only 16.5% of packs contain one, diluting the signal roughly 1:8; and the hypothesis that corrections live in overlapping audio is FALSE, they survive the overlap-free filter at 66.4% against 74.8% for all utterances.
experiments.decision: Do not promote arm B and do not replace artifact-adapter-fixed; no measurement here justifies it. Do not rerun this comparison at a step budget: any future arm comparison must be matched on epochs or on optimizer updates with the dataset size declared, per #49. Every future training run saves intermediate checkpoints and scores them with the EXTERNAL scorer rather than in-training eval, which uses a different normalization (it folds final sigma; the official scorer does not). Gate 6 is not fixed retroactively - the STOP stands - but #48 now has its exact diagnosis: the statistic is degenerate when the net effect approaches zero. Record that the 39 validation windows have now driven two screens, the stopping behaviour and a budget choice; ordinary confidence intervals no longer describe an untouched evaluation set, and any further claim must either say so or use untouched material.
caveats: Levels are not comparable to historical CPU int8 validation numbers; only the paired A/B contrast within this one GPU float16 stack is valid (the results file carries this guard).
The t-statistics across seeds are post-hoc description, not preregistered inference, and n=3 makes them fragile.
Arm A never completed one epoch at either rung, so this experiment does not establish how arm A behaves when trained to convergence.

experiments.title: Epoch-matched clean-pack rerun: contiguous vs contiguous+spliced, 3 seeds
experiments.question: At a budget matched in epochs rather than steps, does the clean-pack recipe beat artifact-adapter-fixed on the 39 frozen validation windows, and does adding jitter-spliced packs help?
experiments.conclusion: The contiguous arm wins in all three seeds; the spliced arm does not. 619 steps (~2 pack epochs), one RTX A4000, every adapter scored by the same external scorer on the same 39 windows with the frozen CONTROL decode config and per-window seed. The incumbent was RE-SCORED on this stack (0.16002); its older 0.1542 came from a different stack and is not comparable. Pre-declared gate (upper bound of the paired meeting-clustered bootstrap CI vs incumbent below zero, Bonferroni 98.33% across three arms, seed 13 pre-declared as shipping seed): cont s13 0.14566 (upper -0.00171 PASS), s29 0.13995 (-0.00595 PASS), s47 0.13895 (-0.00736 PASS); comb s13 0.15255 (+0.01173 FAIL), s29 0.15028 (+0.00752 FAIL), s47 0.14524 (-0.00060 marginal). The combined arm is inconsistent across seeds and does not pass. Head-to-head against its own contiguous twin it is WORSE: +0.00688 [-0.00212,+0.01587] for s13 and +0.01033 [+0.00168,+0.01919] for s29. Insertions rise from 2.3% to 3.0-3.4% while deletions stay flat, but NO cause is established: only the contiguous arm was epoch-matched. Both arms got 619 steps at effective batch 8 = 4,952 samples, which is 2.00 epochs over the 2,475-row contiguous pack but only 0.71 epochs over the 6,984-row combined pack. The combined arm is undertrained relative to its own data, so undertraining and splicing are confounded. The supported claim is only: at an equal number of optimizer updates, adding spliced packs did not help. The contiguous gain runs the other way and is the direction that matters: deletions fall from 0.06196 to 0.03971-0.04450, roughly a third fewer omitted reference tokens, with substitutions flat. 29 of 39 windows improve; the largest single window contributes 24-28% of the effect, clear of the 67% domination seen previously.
experiments.decision: Promote the contiguous clean-pack recipe from validation to testing. Do NOT ship on this evidence alone: these 39 windows are the validation set and have been scored repeatedly. Do not build on the spliced packs without first running them epoch-matched.
caveats: Validation, not test. argos+orestiada have been scored many times across this project; a validation win justifies promotion to testing, not a product claim.
Only 2.5% of pack utterances are corrections, so the packs dilute the correction signal ~1:8 relative to the incumbent's training set. Unresolved.
The incumbent's own recipe was never re-run epoch-matched on its own data, so part of the gap could be the epoch budget rather than the data. Unresolved.
comb_s47 passes the gate marginally (upper -0.00060) while comb_s13 and comb_s29 fail. Quoting comb_s47 alone would be seed selection.

The combined arm was matched in STEPS, not epochs (0.71 vs 2.00) - the same design error this experiment was built to fix, caught by external review after the fact. Whether jitter-splicing helps at a matched epoch budget (~1,746 steps) is UNMEASURED.

experiments.title: Three-system composition on the held-out post-June windows
experiments.question: Does per-column composition of three ASR hypotheses still beat the best single system on 391 windows from meetings no adapter trained on, with the current adapter as the third voter?
experiments.conclusion: Yes, and it has reached the ceiling of selection. W = 0.1202 against Scribe v2 at 0.1377, paired meeting-clustered bootstrap over 117 meetings: -0.0175, 95% CI [-0.0215, -0.0134]. W vs the whole-window oracle is +0.0004, CI [-0.0029, +0.0030] - no method that picks whole hypotheses can do better. The per-column oracle on the same alignment is 0.0611, roughly half of W, so composition is far from its own ceiling. Robust: top 5 windows carry 15.5% of the gain, W wins 98 of 117 meetings, leave-one-meeting-out keeps the delta in [-0.0186, -0.0167].
experiments.decision: Composition, not the adapter, is the deliverable that beats what OpenCouncil runs today. The remaining accuracy in this project is the W-to-column-oracle gap, not more fine-tuning. Next: whether any of this survives with TWO systems, which is what production can afford (exp-2026-08-21-fusion-production).
caveats: oracle_msa is the best path through ONE alignment lattice, and that lattice minimises sum-of-pairs edit cost rather than oracle WER. It bounds this substrate, not the information three transcripts carry. Flagged by Codex review of the plan.

experiments.title: Free screen of the decoder-only training proposal
experiments.question: Are our adapter's substitutions decoder-shaped (homophone misspellings a language model could fix) or acoustic, and how much WER is a decoder-only arm bounded by?
experiments.conclusion: Decoder-shaped, and bounded. 44.6% of our long-word substitutions are within two characters of the right word - but Scribe (41.1%) and Soniox (38.8%) are the same shape, so the distinguishing feature is volume, not shape. The decoder-only-fixable subset is homophone misspellings, where the two spellings sound identical in Greek: 855 of 11,708 substitutions (7.3%), against Scribe's 2.9% and Soniox's 4.5%. Fixing every one of ours is worth -0.0077 WER, about 15% of the 4.18-point gap to Scribe. Most frequent are council vocabulary: απών->απόν and παρών->παρόν 46 times, πίστωσης->πίστοσης, Αργιθέας->Αργυθέας.
experiments.decision: Do not buy GPU for a decoder-only arm on this evidence. Screen the free variant first: post-hoc spelling repair against the short closed list of council vocabulary, which has the same ceiling and costs nothing. If the repair cannot capture the 0.0077, retraining the decoder to capture it is not a good bet. For scale, the composition-to-column-oracle gap on the same windows is 0.0591, nearly eight times this ceiling.
experiments.next_action: Screen the roster/vocabulary spelling repair against the 855 homophone substitutions; no GPU.
caveats: The phonetic folding is a hand-written Greek approximation (ω/ο, η/ι/υ/ει/οι, αι/ε, ς/σ, ντ/δ, μπ/β), not a validated grapheme-to-phoneme model. It will both miss real homophones and merge a few non-homophones, so 7.3% is an estimate with unmeasured error bars.
Agreement-with-OpenCouncil references, so a 'misspelling' here can also be the published transcript's own spelling choice rather than a true error.
The 0.0077 is an oracle: it assumes every homophone substitution is repaired and none is broken.

experiments.title: Token-level decomposition of the adapter's gap to Scribe v2
experiments.question: Where exactly are the 4.18 WER points between our clean-pack adapter and Scribe v2 on the held-out post-June windows, and what is each route to closing them worth?
experiments.conclusion: The gap is substitutions (+0.0533) and deletions (+0.0221); we beat Scribe on insertions (-0.0337). Per reference token: 84.1% both correct, 9.7% only Scribe, 2.2% only ours, 4.0% neither - so the ceiling for catching Scribe by fixing our own errors is 0.0824, but against the full trio our unique contribution is only 0.4% (491 function-word tokens), so the 2.2% is a two-system artefact and is withdrawn. Ranked by recoverable WER: far substitutions 0.0386, near-misses 0.0302, deletions 0.0217, homophones 0.0066. 36% of our deleted tokens disappear in runs of 5+ consecutive words, against Scribe's 19%. The gap is flat across window position, so chunking is not the cause. Samothraki holds 8% of tokens and 24.5% of the gap.
experiments.decision: Do not pursue decoder-only training or chunking-aware decoding as the route to Scribe: the first is bounded at 0.0066 and the second shows no positional signal. The largest recoverable bucket is far substitutions, which needs better listening rather than better spelling. Fusion is the only measured route that already beats Scribe. Next free screens: the cause of the long deletion runs, and why Samothraki costs a quarter of the gap.
experiments.next_action: Screen the 128 long deletion runs and the Samothraki concentration; both are free on the cached substrate.
caveats: Error attribution comes from one Levenshtein backtrace per window; where several alignments cost the same, the substitution/deletion split is arbitrary. Totals are stable, bucket boundaries are not exact.

The 0.0824 'catch Scribe' bound is not a clean oracle: it is 0.0404 (tokens neither system gets) plus 0.0421 (our own insertions, carried over untouched). An oracle free to discard insertions goes lower - the trio's per-column oracle is 0.0611.

Our adapter's unique contribution is 0.4% inside the trio, not 2.2%. The apparent numeral advantage was a formatting convention: Scribe writes number words, Soniox writes digits, the reference uses both. The numeral claim is withdrawn.
Trios carrying the previous adapter (0.1183) or gpt-4o (0.1197) score at least as well as the trio carrying the new one (0.1202). Our adapter's case as third voter is cost, not accuracy.
Agreement-with-OpenCouncil references, so a substitution can be the published transcript's own choice.
Samothraki's 24.5% share is descriptive; no cause is established.

artifacts.description: Supplementary training pack from HParl (Elormiden mirror) at the CALIBRATED gate: align>=0.50 AND dur>=1.5s AND >=3 tokens, clipped-edge rows admitted with edge_clipped=true and weight=0.5. 9,334 rows / 13.16 h (11.66 h weighted), 24.2% edge-clipped, 22.8% complete sentences. caveats: The gate rests on 62 blind human judgements with 6 rows per control - enough to show align>=0.95 was wrong, not enough to fix the exact floor at 0.50.

Judges were told to ignore truncation, so clipped-but-correct rows counted as good. That is why 24.2% of this pack carries weight=0.5 rather than being excluded; a sampler that ignores the weight field trains on them at full strength.

Word guard on the punctuation stage rejected 344/9,835 (3.5%) LLM outputs overall, but the rate is ~7% among the newly admitted lower-alignment rows vs 0.6% at align>=0.95: where Soniox is more wrong, the LLM is more tempted to reword. Rejected rows fall back to deterministic transfer.
One punctuation batch failed to parse as JSON; those rows kept the deterministic transfer.
Out of domain (parliament, not municipal council): stage-1 adaptation input, never in-domain data.
Licence DISPUTED at the mirror (YAML cc-by-4.0 vs its own README CC BY-NC 4.0); CLARIN 1602 not checked at source.

artifacts.description: Arm X, the seam-repairing decode policy, packaged as a runnable configuration rather than an experiment script. Cores of at most 27.0 s; boundary chosen by a three-step ladder (VAD silence >=0.5 s, else the lowest-mean Silero probability valley of >=128 ms below 0.35 within the last 3.0 s, else blind); each core decoded from [core_start-0.5 s, core_end+2.0 s] so every seam is heard from both sides while still fitting one 30 s Whisper window (27.0+0.5+2.0=29.5); the previous cores' text carried as a 64-TOKEN initial_prompt; every word owned by the core containing its own midpoint, margins being context only. Everything else is the frozen CONTROL decode config with word_timestamps=True.
caveats: STATUS IS 'ACTIVE' IN THE SCHEMA SENSE ONLY -- the file exists, is runnable and hashes as recorded. The EVIDENCE behind it is exploratory; see exp-2026-08-20-seam-repair before quoting any number from it.

EXPLORATORY. Packaged so it CAN be run over a benchmark, not because a benchmark has endorsed it. The mechanism checks pass; the quality evidence is 5 windows chosen because arm P fails on them, plus a 39-window exploratory run on windows that generated the hypothesis.
Not validated on contiguous whole-meeting audio. Every measurement so far is on pre-cut ~150 s evaluation windows, so the policy has never chosen a boundary near a real meeting's start or end.

eval/tests/test_decode_x_policy.py asserts the served POLICY constants equal the experiment constants and that the policy reproduces the measured arm's boundaries on a cached window. If that test fails, the served policy has drifted from the measured one and no number attached to it is valid.
The policy hash covers the config only, not the model. Always record artifact-ct2-fixed alongside it.

artifacts.description: Arm P, the silence-cutting decode policy, packaged as a runnable configuration rather than an experiment script. Silero VAD marks silences (>=0.5 s, no speech padding); audio accumulates to at most 29.5 s and is then cut at the LATEST silence midpoint that leaves a piece of at least 5.0 s containing at least 2.5 s of voiced audio, falling back to the latest in-range candidate and then to a blind cut at the ceiling; a final piece under 5.0 s is merged into its predecessor or the shared boundary is moved. Each piece is decoded independently with the frozen CONTROL config and the piece texts are concatenated with segment timestamps offset. No context margins, no initial_prompt, no seam de-duplication -- those are arm X.
caveats: P IS THE BEST MEASURED ARM BY WER, NOT AN ARM THAT PASSED A GATE. WER 0.15893 -> 0.14751, delta -0.01142, CI [-0.02025, -0.00195] excluding zero -- but the preregistered gate of its experiment was on DELETIONS, and the deletion delta -0.00428 has a CI containing zero. The win comes from substitutions. Every text about this policy must say so.
The policy hash covers the config only, not the model. Always record artifact-ct2-fixed alongside it.
The efficacy evidence is the 39 local-CPU windows only. The 247-window GPU run has never been done for P, and the two stacks must never be mixed.

eval/tests/test_decode_p_policy.py asserts the served POLICY constants equal the experiment constants, that the digest is the pinned one, and that the policy reproduces the measured arm's boundaries on a cached window. If it fails, the served policy has drifted from the measured one and no number attached to it is valid.

The served module imports eval/chunking_decode.py rather than copying it, so the splitter itself could change without changing the policy hash. The frozen planner fixture in the test file is what catches that.
The model hash covers model.bin only, which is what the ledger records; the tokenizer and config files beside it are not covered.

boundary kind is a description of WHERE the boundary landed, recomputed from the silence list, not provenance of why the splitter cut there. The splitter's own cut_silence_duration field is carried over unchanged when the short-tail repair moves a boundary and can name a silence seconds away.

capabilities.title: Run the arm X seam-repair decode policy over arbitrary audio
capabilities.purpose: Decode any audio -- a file, a meeting, a whole benchmark -- under the frozen arm X policy, without going through the experiment harness. This is the difference between a result and something that can be run again.
notes: Local CPU int8, roughly 145 s of wall time per 150 s window on the minipc at 16 threads. No GPU, no money, no external API.
verify=True on DecodeX.load() refuses to run unless the CT2 model hashes to artifact-ct2-fixed; an output whose producing model is unknown is not evidence.
The policy returns word timestamps and the list of boundaries with the reason each was chosen (vad_silence / probability_valley / blind), so a bad transcript can be traced back to its segmentation.

capabilities.title: Run the arm P silence-cutting decode policy over arbitrary audio
capabilities.purpose: Decode any audio -- a file, a whole meeting, a benchmark -- under the frozen arm P policy, without going through the experiment harness. P is the best measured decode arm by WER on the 39 frozen windows.
notes: Local CPU int8, 16 threads on the minipc: measured 0.46-0.79x real time on the three conformance windows once the model is loaded, plus a fixed minute or two per process to load the model and hash its 1.5 GB model.bin. No GPU, no money, no external API.
verify=True on DecodeP.load() hashes model.bin in the directory it is about to load and refuses anything that is not artifact-ct2-fixed; overriding model_dir does not bypass it.
`plan` does the segmentation without decoding, so a 64-minute meeting is planned in about 9 s and the forced-cut rate can be inspected before paying for the transcription.
Every internal boundary is returned with its kind (vad_silence / forced), so a bad stretch of transcript can be traced back to its cut.
